title: Frontend: Authentication
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Authentication. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({accept=true}). Model a demo sign-in state using an injected async acceptance flag, not the host app auth. Labelled Email input and Sign in button await Promise resolution, then show Signed in: trimmed email or Sign in failed in [data-testid="session"]. Empty email shows Email required. Signed-in state exposes Sign out and clears session on activation. No tokens, cookies or network.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Separate the form from session state.
alternativeApproaches: Keep a public screen usable during background session refresh while preserving account isolation.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Pending login; rejection; sign-out during login.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
